articles.title: As drug prices in Europe soar, Public Pharma advocates are charting a new course
articles.author: Peoples Health Dispatch
articles.content_excerpt: Health workers, activists, and access to medicines advocates have gathered in Frankfurt on October 22-23 for the 2nd Public Pharma Conference . The event builds on roughly two years of work by the Public Pharma for Europe Coalition , which aims to construct an alternative vision for the region’s pharmaceutical landscape – and to strengthen the links needed to turn that vision into reality. “When we had the first conference in 2024, we realized there are many people practically working on this topic who shared a similar vision and a similar goal,” Frauke Heller from medico international told BreakThrough News . articles.title: “A Spark from the Cockroaches”: Arundhati Roy on India’s Youth Protests & Modi’s Crackdown
articles.content_excerpt: A court in India on Wednesday ordered the release of two leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party, the youth-led movement that has led historic waves of protests in India since the summer. Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were detained amid massive protests last week after they scaled a barricade to enter a site popular for protest, unfurled the national flag and called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Kumar oversaw the deletion of 130 million names from the voter rolls in India since June of last year. articles.title: Drone strikes kill hundreds in just days in Sudan
articles.author: Pavan Kulkarni
articles.content_excerpt: Drone strikes in war-torn Sudan have killed hundreds in just three days. Most of the deaths were in West Kordofan state, including in an area contested with South Sudan, sparking fears of a spillover of the war. The paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) reportedly killed 41 people by striking a gathering of Internally Displaced People (IDPs) near Sudan’s southeastern border with Ethiopia in the Blue Nile state last Friday, October 9. Later on Sunday, October 18, air defenses of the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), which heads the government, intercepted multiple suicide drones launched by the RSF. articles.title: Trump is sunk
articles.author: Tempest National Committee
articles.content_excerpt: T o put it mildly, Trump is not having a good day. He is facing challenges from above: The Federal Reserve increased interest rates against his wishes. The Supreme Court ruled against his attempt to limit voting by mail. Judges have thwarted him on such issues as the Kennedy Center and his attempt to ban news outlets from the White House. Previously loyal Republicans are fleeing now that a Trump endorsement has become a curse . Major far-right media figures such as Tucker Carlson, Marjorie Taylor Greene and Joe Rogan have broken with him. Impeachment and corruption charges are looming. In addition, he is facing discontent from below: His approval ratings are at record lows . According to polls, 65 percent of voters disapprove of Trump, more than twice as many as the 32 percent who approve.

articles.author: Pablo Meriguet
articles.content_excerpt: Last March, the US justice system reopened a case regarding the alleged responsibility of former Cuban President Raúl Castro in the shooting down of small planes belonging to the organization Brothers to the Rescue in 1996. Cuba has categorically rejected the US accusations. The Caribbean nation argues that the accusation is a distortion of the truth, given that Brothers to the Rescue is considered an organization linked to acts of terrorism and provocation against the country’s government. According to Havana , the aircraft were conducting illegal flights over Cuban airspace.
